One of the more interesting stories in the North American session was President Trump's apparent reversal on beef tariffs as the administration looks for ways to bring down sharply higher beef prices. Go to a grocery store in the U.S. and a pound of ground beef can now cost around $10 for an 85/15 blend. Beef prices have risen much faster than overall food inflation, and like gasoline, beef is something American consumers buy in large quantities and notice immediately when prices rise. That brings Brazil into the picture. Brazil is the world's largest beef exporter. The Trump administration has used tariffs both to "generate revenue" and "protect U.S. producers" from foreign competition.
